newsitem.title: PERU: Cameraman arrested after Peru siege raid released.
newsitem.headline: Cameraman arrested after Peru siege raid released.

text.p: A Mexican cameraman arrested at the Japanese embassy in Lima following the explosive raid to end Peru's 126-day hostage crisis was released by a local state prosecutor early on Friday.
Ricardo Clement, who works with Reuters Television in Bogota, Colombia, was detained on Tuesday after following Japanese hostages freed in the dramatic assault on the ambassador's residence.

"Everything happened very quickly. My colleague and I followed a bus straight into the embassy. I got out and started filming and the embassy security detained me," Clement said shortly after his release.

Clement, who had arrived in Lima just hours earlier to cover the final moments of the 18-week drama, spent one night at a local police station and two at the anti-guerrilla police headquarters before being freed.
Clement, who said he had shown his press credentials and offered to leave after embassy guards took his tape, said he still faced a charge of illegal entry onto international property.
Photographers and cameramen from several news agencies were briefly detained on various occasions throughout the standoff due to strict security measures.
